newsitem.title: UK: Palm oil lower in Europe on output and resale talk.
newsitem.headline: Palm oil lower in Europe on output and resale talk.

text.p: Speculation in Malaysia that February palm oil output may be higher than expected put prices under pressure in Europe at midday on Monday.
"No figures are available yet, but some people are saying that production has picked up a lot quicker than expected after the recent long Chinese and Moslem holidays in Malaysia," said a trader.
Traders said there was also talk that Pakistan private sector players were in the market as resellers, putting further pressure on prices.
European traders said they viewed the Malaysian Palm Oil Registration and Licensing Authority (PORLA) data for January, released on Saturday, as neutral.

PORLA put production during January at 576,967 tonnes, 9.57 percent down from December. Exports were put at 551,665 tonnes against 652,874 tonnes in December while stocks were 696,272 tonnes against 794,454.
Lower Chicago futures at the close on Friday were another bearish factor in the market.
At midday crude palm oil cif Europe was offered $7.50 to $2.50 down in a tradeless market.
Among products RBD palm oil was $5 to $7.50 lower while olein was $7.50 to $10 down.
Olein was the only product to see attract any business during the morning with Mar fetching $595 and $590 and Apr $580 and $579.50 a tonne fob Malaysian ports.
Coconut and palmnkernel oil sellers were $2.50 to $5 up with no business reported so far.
In the soft oil sector soy oil was mixed with sellers 0.25 guilders up to 0.50 guilders down while rape oil was 0.50 guilders lower.
